key_insight: OmniCapBench proposes a deeper, more structured way to evaluate audio-visual captioning in multimodal LLMs, aiming to reveal fine-grained strengths and failure modes instead of only judging overall caption quality.
problem_solved: Current audio-visual captioning benchmarks force a trade-off between broad coverage and precise localization. Whole-caption scores miss where errors occur, local probes lack full coverage, and LLM-based judges can be inconsistent.
method: Builds a deep-structured evaluation framework for fine-grained audio-visual captioning.
Combines broader caption-level assessment with localized probes to diagnose specific audio-visual reasoning capabilities.
Aims to reduce reliance on unstable unconstrained LLM judging by using a more systematic benchmark design.
impact: This benchmark helps researchers and practitioners measure multimodal models more reliably and identify exactly where they fail in audio-visual understanding. That makes it easier to compare models, debug weaknesses, and track progress toward stronger continuous audio-visual reasoning.

paper_title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
paper_authors: Zhongyu Yang, Jiale Tao, Ruitao Chen, Zuhao Yang, Yingfang Yuan
